# instruction.md

# AI Impact on the Global Job Market: Trend Analysis Report

## Overview

You are tasked with producing a comprehensive trend analysis report examining how AI automation is reshaping the global job market from 2015 to 2035. The report covers automation risk, salary dynamics, skill demand, and job survival prospects across roles, countries, and experience levels. The target audience is **executive leadership and workforce strategists** — people who need clear, data-driven insights to make decisions about talent investment, reskilling programs, and strategic workforce planning. The tone should be professional, data-forward, and actionable throughout.

## Key Priorities

- **Trend analysis is the backbone of this report.** Every major KPI — AI risk scores, median salaries, job openings, skill demand — should be examined over time. Year-over-year movement matters more than static snapshots.
- **The Executive Overview must stand on its own.** An executive should be able to read only that section and walk away with the three to five most critical takeaways.
- **Salary × automation risk correlation** is a high-value insight. Make sure the Salary Trends section explicitly addresses how compensation relates to AI risk levels.
- **Strategic Recommendations must be grounded in the data.** Every recommendation should trace back to a specific finding — no generic advice.
- Visualizations should be clean, well-labeled, and designed for quick comprehension by non-technical readers. Use charts that highlight trends and comparisons effectively.

## Data Integrity

**Absolutely no fabrication.** Every number, percentage, and trend cited in the report must be derived directly from `data.csv`. If the data is insufficient to support a claim, note the limitation rather than inventing figures.

## Output

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for report requirements, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final report to `/app/output/`. Use the filename and format specified in the instruction above.
2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `report.tone`, `report.audience`, etc., use them to choose color schemes, chart types, and layout styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

3	## About the Dataset
4	
5	This dataset explores the evolving relationship between Artificial Intelligence, global job markets, skills, and salaries over a 21-year horizon from 2015 to 2035. It is sourced from Kaggle (shree0910/ai-job-risk-and-salary-dataset-20152035) and is designed for analytical, educational, and modeling purposes. The data is synthetically generated using realistic assumptions inspired by global job market patterns, AI adoption rates, and salary distributions.
6	
7	- **Source:** Kaggle
8	- **Rows:** 12,343
9	- **Columns:** 13
10	- **Time Range:** 2015–2035
11	- **Data Type:** Synthetic + Trend-Based (Realistic Simulation)
12	
13	## Column Schema
14	
15	| Column Name | Type | Description |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `job_title` | String | The job role or occupation (e.g., Data Scientist, Software Engineer, Data Analyst). Represents distinct career categories in the dataset. |
18	| `country` | String | The country where the job is located (e.g., USA, India, Canada). Enables geographic comparisons. |
19	| `experience_level` | String | Professional experience tier. Expected values include "Entry", "Mid", and "Senior". |
20	| `education_level` | String | Highest education attainment. Expected values include "Bachelor", "Master", and "PhD". |
21	| `year` | Integer | The calendar year of the record, ranging from 2015 to 2035. Supports time-series and trend analysis. |
22	| `salary` | Float | Annual salary in USD. Values vary significantly by country, role, and experience level. |
23	| `ai_risk_score` | Float | A continuous score between 0 and 1 representing the probability that the job will be significantly impacted or automated by AI. Higher values indicate greater risk. |
24	| `primary_skill` | String | The most important or representative skill for the job (e.g., Python, Java, SQL). Indicates the core competency associated with the role. |
25	| `skill_demand_score` | Integer | A score (likely 0–100) reflecting how in-demand the primary skill is in the job market for that year. |
26	| `job_openings` | Integer | The number of job openings available for the role in the given country and year. |
27	| `job_survival_class` | Integer | A classification target variable indicating job survival prospects. Observed values include 0 (at risk / unlikely to survive), 1 (moderate survival), and 2 (strong survival). |
28	| `salary_bucket` | String | A categorical bucketing of the salary value. Expected values include "Low", "Medium", and "High". |
29	| `ai_risk_category` | String | A categorical label derived from the ai_risk_score. Expected values include "Low Risk", "Medium Risk", and "High Risk". |
30	
31	## Key Analytical Notes
32	
33	- **Target Variable:** `job_survival_class` serves as a classification target for machine learning and can also be used as a key segmentation variable in reporting. Values 0, 1, and 2 represent increasing levels of job resilience against AI disruption.
34	- **Derived Columns:** `salary_bucket` and `ai_risk_category` are pre-computed categorical columns derived from `salary` and `ai_risk_score` respectively. These are visualization-ready and useful for grouping and filtering.
35	- **Time Dimension:** The dataset spans both historical (2015–2024) and projected future (2025–2035) periods. Analysts should note that future years represent simulated projections, not observed data.
36	- **Geographic Scope:** Multiple countries are represented, enabling cross-country salary and risk comparisons. Salary values are in USD and should be interpreted with awareness of purchasing power differences.
37	- **Data Quality:** As a synthetic dataset, there are no expected missing values or encoding issues. All columns are consistently populated across the full 12,343 rows.
38	
39	## Intended Use
40	
41	This dataset is well-suited for trend analysis, workforce planning insights, interactive dashboard creation, and predictive modeling around AI's impact on employment.

# AI Job Impact & Salary Dataset (2015–2035)

## About the Dataset

This dataset explores the evolving relationship between Artificial Intelligence, global job markets, skills, and salaries over a 21-year horizon from 2015 to 2035. It is sourced from Kaggle (shree0910/ai-job-risk-and-salary-dataset-20152035) and is designed for analytical, educational, and modeling purposes. The data is synthetically generated using realistic assumptions inspired by global job market patterns, AI adoption rates, and salary distributions.

- **Source:** Kaggle
- **Rows:** 12,343
- **Columns:** 13
- **Time Range:** 2015–2035
- **Data Type:** Synthetic + Trend-Based (Realistic Simulation)

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job_title` | String | The job role or occupation (e.g., Data Scientist, Software Engineer, Data Analyst). Represents distinct career categories in the dataset. |
| `country` | String | The country where the job is located (e.g., USA, India, Canada). Enables geographic comparisons. |

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the AI Impact on Global Job Market trend analysis report."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import json

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv("/app/benchmark/data.csv")

# ── Color palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PALETTE = {
    "primary": "#1a237e",
    "secondary": "#0d47a1",
    "accent": "#ff6f00",
    "danger": "#c62828",
    "warning": "#f9a825",
    "success": "#2e7d32",
    "surface": "#f5f5f5",
    "text": "#212121",
    "muted": "#757575",
    "border": "#e0e0e0",
}
RISK_COLORS = {"Low Risk": "#2e7d32", "Medium Risk": "#f9a825", "High Risk": "#c62828"}
SURVIVAL_COLORS = {0: "#c62828", 1: "#f9a825", 2: "#2e7d32"}

# ── Helper: format large numbers ───────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_k(v):
    if abs(v) >= 1_000_000:
        return f"${v/1_000_000:.1f}M"
    if abs(v) >= 1_000:
        return f"${v/1_000:.0f}K"
    return f"${v:.0f}"

# ── Analysis functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def kpi_summary():
    """Core KPIs across the full dataset."""
    return {
        "total_rows": len(df),
        "years": f"{df['year'].min()}–{df['year'].max()}",
        "countries": df["country"].nunique(),
        "job_titles": df["job_title"].nunique(),
        "primary_skills": df["primary_skill"].nunique(),
        "mean_ai_risk": df["ai_risk_score"].mean(),
        "median_salary": df["salary"].median(),
        "survival_rate": (df["job_survival_class"] >= 1).mean(),
        "mean_skill_demand": df["skill_demand_score"].mean(),
        "total_openings": df["job_openings"].sum(),
    }


def risk_trend_by_year():
    """Average AI risk score by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_by_job_title():
    """Mean AI risk score by job title, sorted."""
    grp = df.groupby("job_title")["ai_risk_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index()
    grp = grp.sort_values("mean", ascending=True)
    return grp


def risk_by_country():
    """Mean AI risk score by country."""
    return df.groupby("country")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index().sort_values("ai_risk_score")


def risk_by_experience():
    """Mean AI risk score by experience level."""
    return df.groupby("experience_level")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_category_distribution():
    """Count by ai_risk_category."""
    return df["ai_risk_category"].value_counts().reset_index()


def salary_trend_by_year():
    """Median salary by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_job_country():
    """Median salary by job title and country."""
    return df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_experience_year():
    """Median salary by experience level and year."""
    return df.groupby(["year", "experience_level"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_risk_category():
    """Median salary by AI risk category."""
    return df.groupby("ai_risk_category")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_risk_correlation():
    """Salary vs AI risk score scatter data."""
    return df.groupby("job_title").agg(
        mean_salary=("salary", "median"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("job_title", "count"),
    ).reset_index()


def skill_demand_trend():
    """Average skill demand score by year for top skills."""
    top_skills = df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].mean().nlargest(10).index
    return df[df["primary_skill"].isin(top_skills)].groupby(
        ["year", "primary_skill"]
    )["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_demand_by_skill():
    """Average skill demand score by primary skill."""
    return df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index().sort_values("mean", ascending=False)


def skill_vs_survival():
    """Average skill demand by survival class."""
    return df.groupby("job_survival_class")["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_vs_risk():
    """Top skills by demand and their associated risk."""
    grp = df.groupby("primary_skill").agg(
        mean_demand=("skill_demand_score", "mean"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("primary_skill", "count"),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp.sort_values("mean_demand", ascending=False).head(15)


def survival_trend():
    """Survival rate over time."""
    grp = df.groupby("year").agg(
        survival_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()),
        strong_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x == 2).mean()),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp


def openings_trend():
    """Total job openings by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index()


def openings_by_job_title():
    """Total job openings by job title."""
    return df.groupby("job_title")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index().sort_values("job_openings", ascending=False)


def survival_by_job_country():
    """Survival rate by job title and country."""
    grp = df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["job_survival_class"].apply(
        lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()
    ).reset_index()
    grp.columns = ["job_title", "country", "survival_rate"]
    return grp.sort_values("survival_rate", ascending=False)


def survival_by_education():
    """Survival rate by education level."""
    return df.groupby("education_level")["job_survival_class"].apply(
        lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()
    ).reset_index()


def risk_salary_heatmap_data():
    """Pivot of job_title x experience_level avg salary."""
    return df.pivot_table(
        values="salary", index="job_title", columns="experience_level", aggfunc="median"
    )


# ── Chart builders ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fig_salary_bucket_trend():
    """Stacked area chart of salary bucket distribution over time."""
    grp = df.groupby(["year", "salary_bucket"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
    grp_pct = grp.copy()
    totals = grp.groupby("year")["count"].sum().reset_index()
    grp_pct = grp_pct.merge(totals, on="year", suffixes=("", "_total"))
    grp_pct["pct"] = grp_pct["count"] / grp_pct["count_total"] * 100

    bucket_colors = {"Low": "#ef5350", "Medium": "#ffb300", "High": "#1b5e20"}
    fig = go.Figure()
    for bucket in ["Low", "Medium", "High"]:
        sub = grp_pct[grp_pct["salary_bucket"] == bucket]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=sub["year"], y=sub["pct"],
            mode="lines", stackgroup="one", name=bucket,
            line=dict(width=0), fillcolor=bucket_colors[bucket],
        ))
    fig.update_layout(
        title="Salary Bucket Distribution Over Time (%)",
        xaxis_title="Year", yaxis_title="Percentage of Records",
        template="plotly_white", height=380,
        margin=dict(l=40, r=20, t=50, b=40),
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1),
    )
    return fig

def fig_salary_bucket_trend():
    """Stacked area chart of salary bucket distribution over time."""
    grp = df.groupby(["year", "salary_bucket"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
    grp_pct = grp.copy()
    totals = grp.groupby("year")["count"].sum().reset_index()
    grp_pct = grp_pct.merge(totals, on="year", suffixes=("", "_total"))
    grp_pct["pct"] = grp_pct["count"] / grp_pct["count_total"] * 100

    bucket_colors = {"Low": "#ef5350", "Medium": "#ffb300", "High": "#1b5e20"}
    fig = go.Figure()
    for bucket in ["Low", "Medium", "High"]:
        sub = grp_pct[grp_pct["salary_bucket"] == bucket]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=sub["year"], y=sub["pct"],
            mode="lines", stackgroup="one", name=bucket,
            line=dict(width=0), fillcolor=bucket_colors[bucket],
        ))
    fig.update_layout(
        title="Salary Bucket Distribution Over Time (%)",
        xaxis_title="Year", yaxis_title="Percentage of Records",
        template="plotly_white", height=380,
        margin=dict(l=40, r=20, t=50, b=40),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the AI Impact on Global Job Market trend analysis report."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import json

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv("/app/benchmark/data.csv")

# ── Color palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PALETTE = {
    "primary": "#1a237e",
    "secondary": "#0d47a1",
    "accent": "#ff6f00",
    "danger": "#c62828",
    "warning": "#f9a825",
    "success": "#2e7d32",
    "surface": "#f5f5f5",
    "text": "#212121",
    "muted": "#757575",
    "border": "#e0e0e0",
}
RISK_COLORS = {"Low Risk": "#2e7d32", "Medium Risk": "#f9a825", "High Risk": "#c62828"}
SURVIVAL_COLORS = {0: "#c62828", 1: "#f9a825", 2: "#2e7d32"}

# ── Helper: format large numbers ───────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_k(v):
    if abs(v) >= 1_000_000:
        return f"${v/1_000_000:.1f}M"
    if abs(v) >= 1_000:
        return f"${v/1_000:.0f}K"
    return f"${v:.0f}"

# ── Analysis functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def kpi_summary():
    """Core KPIs across the full dataset."""
    return {
        "total_rows": len(df),
        "years": f"{df['year'].min()}–{df['year'].max()}",
        "countries": df["country"].nunique(),
        "job_titles": df["job_title"].nunique(),
        "primary_skills": df["primary_skill"].nunique(),
        "mean_ai_risk": df["ai_risk_score"].mean(),
        "median_salary": df["salary"].median(),
        "survival_rate": (df["job_survival_class"] >= 1).mean(),
        "mean_skill_demand": df["skill_demand_score"].mean(),
        "total_openings": df["job_openings"].sum(),
    }


def risk_trend_by_year():
    """Average AI risk score by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_by_job_title():
    """Mean AI risk score by job title, sorted."""
    grp = df.groupby("job_title")["ai_risk_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index()
    grp = grp.sort_values("mean", ascending=True)
    return grp


def risk_by_country():
    """Mean AI risk score by country."""
    return df.groupby("country")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index().sort_values("ai_risk_score")


def risk_by_experience():
    """Mean AI risk score by experience level."""
    return df.groupby("experience_level")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_category_distribution():
    """Count by ai_risk_category."""
    return df["ai_risk_category"].value_counts().reset_index()


def salary_trend_by_year():
    """Median salary by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_job_country():
    """Median salary by job title and country."""
    return df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_experience_year():
    """Median salary by experience level and year."""
    return df.groupby(["year", "experience_level"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_risk_category():
    """Median salary by AI risk category."""
    return df.groupby("ai_risk_category")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_risk_correlation():
    """Salary vs AI risk score scatter data."""
    return df.groupby("job_title").agg(
        mean_salary=("salary", "median"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("job_title", "count"),
    ).reset_index()


def skill_demand_trend():
    """Average skill demand score by year for top skills."""
    top_skills = df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].mean().nlargest(10).index
    return df[df["primary_skill"].isin(top_skills)].groupby(
        ["year", "primary_skill"]
    )["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_demand_by_skill():
    """Average skill demand score by primary skill."""
    return df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index().sort_values("mean", ascending=False)


def skill_vs_survival():
    """Average skill demand by survival class."""
    return df.groupby("job_survival_class")["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_vs_risk():
    """Top skills by demand and their associated risk."""
    grp = df.groupby("primary_skill").agg(
        mean_demand=("skill_demand_score", "mean"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("primary_skill", "count"),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp.sort_values("mean_demand", ascending=False).head(15)


def survival_trend():
    """Survival rate over time."""
    grp = df.groupby("year").agg(
        survival_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()),
        strong_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x == 2).mean()),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp


def openings_trend():
    """Total job openings by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index()


def openings_by_job_title():
    """Total job openings by job title."""
    return df.groupby("job_title")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index().sort_values("job_openings", ascending=False)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the AI Impact on Global Job Market trend analysis report."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import json

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv("/app/benchmark/data.csv")

# ── Color palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PALETTE = {
    "primary": "#1a237e",
    "secondary": "#0d47a1",
    "accent": "#ff6f00",
    "danger": "#c62828",
    "warning": "#f9a825",
    "success": "#2e7d32",
    "surface": "#f5f5f5",
    "text": "#212121",
    "muted": "#757575",
    "border": "#e0e0e0",
}
RISK_COLORS = {"Low Risk": "#2e7d32", "Medium Risk": "#f9a825", "High Risk": "#c62828"}
SURVIVAL_COLORS = {0: "#c62828", 1: "#f9a825", 2: "#2e7d32"}

# ── Helper: format large numbers ───────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_k(v):
    if abs(v) >= 1_000_000:
        return f"${v/1_000_000:.1f}M"
    if abs(v) >= 1_000:
        return f"${v/1_000:.0f}K"
    return f"${v:.0f}"

# ── Analysis functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def kpi_summary():
    """Core KPIs across the full dataset."""
    return {
        "total_rows": len(df),
        "years": f"{df['year'].min()}–{df['year'].max()}",
        "countries": df["country"].nunique(),
        "job_titles": df["job_title"].nunique(),
        "primary_skills": df["primary_skill"].nunique(),
        "mean_ai_risk": df["ai_risk_score"].mean(),
        "median_salary": df["salary"].median(),
        "survival_rate": (df["job_survival_class"] >= 1).mean(),
        "mean_skill_demand": df["skill_demand_score"].mean(),
        "total_openings": df["job_openings"].sum(),
    }


def risk_trend_by_year():
    """Average AI risk score by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_by_job_title():
    """Mean AI risk score by job title, sorted."""
    grp = df.groupby("job_title")["ai_risk_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index()
    grp = grp.sort_values("mean", ascending=True)
    return grp


def risk_by_country():
    """Mean AI risk score by country."""
    return df.groupby("country")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index().sort_values("ai_risk_score")


def risk_by_experience():
    """Mean AI risk score by experience level."""
    return df.groupby("experience_level")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_category_distribution():
    """Count by ai_risk_category."""
    return df["ai_risk_category"].value_counts().reset_index()


def salary_trend_by_year():
    """Median salary by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_job_country():
    """Median salary by job title and country."""
    return df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_experience_year():
    """Median salary by experience level and year."""
    return df.groupby(["year", "experience_level"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_risk_category():
    """Median salary by AI risk category."""
    return df.groupby("ai_risk_category")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_risk_correlation():
    """Salary vs AI risk score scatter data."""
    return df.groupby("job_title").agg(
        mean_salary=("salary", "median"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("job_title", "count"),
    ).reset_index()


def skill_demand_trend():
    """Average skill demand score by year for top skills."""
    top_skills = df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].mean().nlargest(10).index
    return df[df["primary_skill"].isin(top_skills)].groupby(
        ["year", "primary_skill"]
    )["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_demand_by_skill():
    """Average skill demand score by primary skill."""
    return df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index().sort_values("mean", ascending=False)


def skill_vs_survival():
    """Average skill demand by survival class."""
    return df.groupby("job_survival_class")["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_vs_risk():
    """Top skills by demand and their associated risk."""
    grp = df.groupby("primary_skill").agg(
        mean_demand=("skill_demand_score", "mean"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("primary_skill", "count"),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp.sort_values("mean_demand", ascending=False).head(15)


def survival_trend():
    """Survival rate over time."""
    grp = df.groupby("year").agg(
        survival_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the AI Impact on Global Job Market trend analysis report."""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import json

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv("/app/benchmark/data.csv")

# ── Color palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PALETTE = {
    "primary": "#1a237e",
    "secondary": "#0d47a1",
    "accent": "#ff6f00",
    "danger": "#c62828",
    "warning": "#f9a825",
    "success": "#2e7d32",
    "surface": "#f5f5f5",
    "text": "#212121",
    "muted": "#757575",
    "border": "#e0e0e0",
}
RISK_COLORS = {"Low Risk": "#2e7d32", "Medium Risk": "#f9a825", "High Risk": "#c62828"}
SURVIVAL_COLORS = {0: "#c62828", 1: "#f9a825", 2: "#2e7d32"}

# ── Helper: format large numbers ───────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_k(v):
    if abs(v) >= 1_000_000:
        return f"${v/1_000_000:.1f}M"
    if abs(v) >= 1_000:
        return f"${v/1_000:.0f}K"
    return f"${v:.0f}"

# ── Analysis functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def kpi_summary():
    """Core KPIs across the full dataset."""
    return {
        "total_rows": len(df),
        "years": f"{df['year'].min()}–{df['year'].max()}",
        "countries": df["country"].nunique(),
        "job_titles": df["job_title"].nunique(),
        "primary_skills": df["primary_skill"].nunique(),
        "mean_ai_risk": df["ai_risk_score"].mean(),
        "median_salary": df["salary"].median(),
        "survival_rate": (df["job_survival_class"] >= 1).mean(),
        "mean_skill_demand": df["skill_demand_score"].mean(),
        "total_openings": df["job_openings"].sum(),
    }


def risk_trend_by_year():
    """Average AI risk score by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_by_job_title():
    """Mean AI risk score by job title, sorted."""
    grp = df.groupby("job_title")["ai_risk_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index()
    grp = grp.sort_values("mean", ascending=True)
    return grp


def risk_by_country():
    """Mean AI risk score by country."""
    return df.groupby("country")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index().sort_values("ai_risk_score")


def risk_by_experience():
    """Mean AI risk score by experience level."""
    return df.groupby("experience_level")["ai_risk_score"].mean().reset_index()


def risk_category_distribution():
    """Count by ai_risk_category."""
    return df["ai_risk_category"].value_counts().reset_index()


def salary_trend_by_year():
    """Median salary by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_job_country():
    """Median salary by job title and country."""
    return df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_experience_year():
    """Median salary by experience level and year."""
    return df.groupby(["year", "experience_level"])["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_by_risk_category():
    """Median salary by AI risk category."""
    return df.groupby("ai_risk_category")["salary"].median().reset_index()


def salary_risk_correlation():
    """Salary vs AI risk score scatter data."""
    return df.groupby("job_title").agg(
        mean_salary=("salary", "median"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("job_title", "count"),
    ).reset_index()


def skill_demand_trend():
    """Average skill demand score by year for top skills."""
    top_skills = df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].mean().nlargest(10).index
    return df[df["primary_skill"].isin(top_skills)].groupby(
        ["year", "primary_skill"]
    )["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_demand_by_skill():
    """Average skill demand score by primary skill."""
    return df.groupby("primary_skill")["skill_demand_score"].agg(["mean", "count"]).reset_index().sort_values("mean", ascending=False)


def skill_vs_survival():
    """Average skill demand by survival class."""
    return df.groupby("job_survival_class")["skill_demand_score"].mean().reset_index()


def skill_vs_risk():
    """Top skills by demand and their associated risk."""
    grp = df.groupby("primary_skill").agg(
        mean_demand=("skill_demand_score", "mean"),
        mean_risk=("ai_risk_score", "mean"),
        count=("primary_skill", "count"),
    ).reset_index()

def survival_trend():
    """Survival rate over time."""
    grp = df.groupby("year").agg(
        survival_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x >= 1).mean()),
        strong_rate=("job_survival_class", lambda x: (x == 2).mean()),
    ).reset_index()
    return grp


def openings_trend():
    """Total job openings by year."""
    return df.groupby("year")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index()


def openings_by_job_title():
    """Total job openings by job title."""
    return df.groupby("job_title")["job_openings"].sum().reset_index().sort_values("job_openings", ascending=False)


def survival_by_job_country():

    grp = df.groupby(["job_title", "country"])["job_survival_class"].apply(

    grp.columns = ["job_title", "country", "survival_rate"]

def survival_by_education():

    return df.groupby("education_level")["job_survival_class"].apply(

<!-- COVER -->
<header class="cover">
  <div class="container">
    <h1>AI Impact on the Global Job Market</h1>
    <p class="subtitle">Risk, Salary & Skills Trend Analysis (2015–2035)</p>
    <p class="meta">
      <span>Dataset: {kpis['total_rows']:,} records</span>
      <span>Period: {kpis['years']}</span>
      <span>{kpis['countries']} Countries</span>
      <span>{kpis['job_titles']} Job Roles</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</header>

<div class="container">
<!-- KPI Ribbon -->
<div class="kpi-ribbon">
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-value">{kpis['mean_ai_risk']:.2f}</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Avg AI Risk Score (0–1)</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_k(kpis['median_salary'])}</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Global Median Salary</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-value">{kpis['survival_rate']*100:.1f}%</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Job Survival Rate</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-value">{kpis['mean_skill_demand']:.1f}</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Avg Skill Demand (0–100)</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-value">{kpis['total_openings']/1e9:.2f}B</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Total Job Openings</div>
  </div>
</div>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 1: Executive Overview -->
<section id="executive-overview">
<div class="container">
<h2 class="section-title">1. Executive Overview</h2>
<p class="section-intro">
  This report analyzes {kpis['total_rows']:,} data records spanning {kpis['years']} across {kpis['countries']} countries and {kpis['job_titles']} job titles
  to assess how AI automation is reshaping the global workforce. The dataset covers both historical trends (2015–2024) and forward-looking projections (2025–2035),
  enabling a full-spectrum view of automation risk, salary dynamics, skill demand, and job survival prospects.
</p>

<div class="callout">
  <strong>Key Takeaway:</strong> AI risk scores have risen from {risk_data.iloc[0]['ai_risk_score']:.2f} in 2015 to {risk_data.iloc[-1]['ai_risk_score']:.2f} in 2035 —
  a {risk_change*100:.1f} percentage-point increase over 21 years. However, the job survival rate remains above {kpis['survival_rate']*100:.0f}%,
  indicating that while automation pressure is intensifying, most roles are adapting rather than disappearing. The critical differentiators for survival
  are <strong>skill relevance</strong> (high-demand skills correlate strongly with survival) and <strong>specialized expertise</strong>
  (Senior and PhD-level roles show lower risk and higher compensation).
</div>

<div class="insight-grid">
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Most Automatable Role</h4>
    <p><strong>{top_risk_job['job_title']}</strong> carries the highest mean AI risk score at {top_risk_job['mean']:.2f},
    reflecting its reliance on routine, rules-based tasks that AI systems increasingly handle.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Most Resilient Role</h4>
    <p><strong>{low_risk_job['job_title']}</strong> shows the lowest AI risk ({low_risk_job['mean']:.2f}),
    benefiting from the need for deep domain expertise, creative problem-solving, and human judgment.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Salary–Risk Divergence</h4>
    <p>Low-risk roles command a median salary of <strong>{fmt_k(low_risk_salary)}</strong> vs. <strong>{fmt_k(high_risk_salary)}</strong> for high-risk roles —
    a <strong>{salary_gap_pct:.0f}% premium</strong> for AI-resilient positions.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Skill That Future-Proofs</h4>
    <p><strong>{top_skill['primary_skill']}</strong> leads all skills with a mean demand score of {top_skill['mean']:.1f},
    and skills in the top demand quartile are {skill_vs_survival().iloc[-1]['skill_demand_score']/skill_vs_survival().iloc[0]['skill_demand_score']:.1f}x
    more likely to be associated with strong survival outcomes.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- SECTION 2: AI Automation Risk Landscape -->
<section class="alt" id="automation-risk-landscape">
<div class="container">
<h2 class="section-title">2. AI Automation Risk Landscape</h2>
<p class="section-intro">
  This section examines how AI risk scores are distributed across job titles, countries, experience levels, and education tiers.
  The analysis identifies which segments face the greatest automation headwinds — and which are structurally more insulated.
</p>

<!-- Risk trend over time -->
<div class="chart-card">
  {charts["risk_trend"]}
</div>

<div class="insight-grid">
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Historical vs. Projected</h4>
    <p>From 2015–2024, the average AI risk score rose gradually from {risk_data[risk_data['year']<=2024].iloc[0]['ai_risk_score']:.2f}
    to {risk_data[risk_data['year']<=2024].iloc[-1]['ai_risk_score']:.2f}. Projections through 2035 show continued acceleration,
    reaching {risk_latest['ai_risk_score']:.2f} — reflecting the compounding effect of generative AI, autonomous systems,
    and broader automation adoption.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Inflection Point (2023–2025)</h4>
    <p>The risk trajectory steepens noticeably around 2023–2025, coinciding with the mainstream emergence of large language models
    and generative AI. This inflection marks a shift from narrow-task automation toward broader cognitive task displacement.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Risk by job & risk by country side by side -->
<div class="chart-row">
  <div class="chart-card">
    {charts["risk_by_job"]}
  </div>
  <div class="chart-card">
    {charts["risk_by_country"]}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Risk by experience & education -->
<div class="chart-row">
  <div class="chart-card">
    {charts["risk_by_exp"]}
  </div>
  <div class="chart-card">
    {charts["risk_by_edu"]}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Risk category distribution -->
<div class="chart-card">
  {charts["risk_cat_dist"]}
</div>

<div class="insight-grid">
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Experience as a Shield</h4>
    <p>Senior roles consistently show lower AI risk scores than Entry and Mid-level positions.
    This pattern reflects that AI currently augments rather than replaces experienced professionals —
    automating routine tasks while the strategic, judgment-intensive aspects of senior roles remain human-led.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Education Matters — With Nuance</h4>
    <p>PhD holders have lower AI risk on average, but the effect varies by role.
    For highly technical fields (AI Researcher, ML Engineer), advanced degrees correlate with lower risk.
    For Business Analyst and similar roles, even advanced education does not fully offset high automation exposure.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Geographic Disparities</h4>
    <p>{high_risk_country['country']} shows the highest mean risk ({high_risk_country['ai_risk_score']:.2f}),
    while {low_risk_country['country']} shows the lowest ({low_risk_country['ai_risk_score']:.2f}).
    Countries with higher concentrations of knowledge-worker roles and service-based economies face different automation profiles
    than those with diverse industrial mixes.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- SECTION 3: Salary Trends -->
<section id="salary-trends">
<div class="container">
<h2 class="section-title">3. Salary Trends & Segmentation</h2>
<p class="section-intro">
  Compensation dynamics offer a critical lens on AI's labor-market impact. This section traces median salary evolution across time,
  experience levels, countries, and risk categories — with particular emphasis on how pay relates to automation risk.
</p>

<div class="chart-card">
  {charts["salary_trend"]}
</div>

<div class="callout">
  <strong>Salary–Risk Correlation:</strong> A clear inverse relationship emerges between salary and AI risk.
  Low-risk roles command a median salary of <strong>{fmt_k(low_risk_salary)}</strong> — {salary_gap_pct:.0f}% higher than the
  <strong>{fmt_k(high_risk_salary)}</strong> median for high-risk roles. The market is pricing AI resilience at a substantial premium,
  and this gap is projected to widen through 2035 as demand for automation-proof skills intensifies.
</div>

<div class="chart-row">
  <div class="chart-card">
    {charts["salary_by_exp"]}

<div class="chart-card">

  </div>

<div class="insight-grid">

    complex decision-making that senior talent provides — capabilities that remain difficult to automate.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Salary Bucket Shifts</h4>
    <p>The proportion of jobs in the "High" salary bucket has shifted over time, reflecting both inflation
    adjustments and the growing market value of technical expertise. The "Low" bucket share has declined
    in some countries but persists in roles with high automation exposure.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<p class="section-intro">

<div class="chart-card">

</div>

    <p>Skills directly associated with AI development — Python, Deep Learning, TensorFlow — command the highest

  <div class="insight-box">

  <div class="insight-box">
    <h4>Routine Skill Decline</h4>
    <p>Skills associated with routine data processing and rules-based analysis (SQL, Excel) show flatter demand

    consistent with their higher automation exposure.</p>

</div>
